evidence.reason: Line 637 treats every ancestor case as success, including when head is strictly older than latest. In that case fetch returns the older head and its stale values even though the validated checkpoint has already advanced. A concurrent publisher can then build a commit on the stale head; if the remote branch is at that older head, the non-force push can append it, bypassing the line-622 rollback guard, and a later fetch rejects it because it does not descend from the checkpoint. The equal-head case is safe; a strict ancestor should retry within a bound or raise IntegrityError. This is a correctness defect in the existing fetch/checkpoint behavior, not a new requirement.
